opening: The record concerns a conservation workshop tracing a damaged artifact through several rooms. By the time investigators reconstructed the treatment that stabilized the artifact, casual impressions had produced several plausible candidates. The reviewers therefore used only the local rules stated in the surviving record.

scenes.prose: Before comparing names, the panel read the governing notes aloud. For this incident, the board declared the certified restoration lead protocol active; ordinary rank and reputation did not count. The panel fixed one shared status scale for the whole inquiry: dormant counted as 0; waking counted as 1; clear counted as 2; stable counted as 3; latent counted as 4; open counted as 5. The local tally began at 12. In order it used relation, temporal, causal, spatial, sequence, and protocol statuses with coefficients 13, 2, 3, 7, 5, 11. At each stream, the panel squared the current tally, added that stream's coefficient times its status value, and kept the remainder modulo 97. It made three passes: first in the stated order, then in reverse order with the coefficients reversed, then once more in the stated order with the coefficient list rotated one place left. Without resetting the tally, it repeated that complete three-pass cycle 121 times.
scenes.title: Reconstruction 1

scenes.prose: The inquiry moved from recollection to checked records. When the pairing sheet was recovered, Val Sato's apprentice lineage stood at open. Even the damaged roster still marked Winter Cohen's apprentice lineage as latent. A clock-backed entry listed Finley Meier's work interval as latent. The chemical response that followed Parker Meier registered as stable. Causal review marked Oakley Brooks's chemical response latent. Door and route checks placed Val Sato's workshop room at waking. Witnesses in the corridor put Winter Cohen's workshop room at clear. Reconstruction kept Finley Meier's treatment order at waking. A close photograph of the token set Parker Meier's tool stamp to waking. At final count, Oakley Brooks's tool stamp remained dormant.
scenes.title: Reconstruction 2

scenes.prose: The inquiry moved from recollection to checked records. A witness who checked the roster left Parker Meier with a clear apprentice lineage. On the sealed worksheet, clerks wrote dormant beside Oakley Brooks's apprentice lineage. Clocked entries put Val Sato's work interval at stable. The sequence sheet showed Winter Cohen's work interval as waking. Downstream checks tied Finley Meier to a open chemical response. A movement sketch marked Parker Meier's workshop room as open. The route ledger tied Oakley Brooks's workshop room to latent. In the ordered log, Val Sato's treatment order appeared as open. The ordered sheet showed Winter Cohen's treatment order as dormant. Inventory counted Finley Meier's tool stamp as stable.
scenes.title: Reconstruction 3

scenes.prose: The inquiry moved from recollection to checked records. In the earlier pairing note, Finley Meier carried a waking apprentice lineage. After the timesheet review, Parker Meier's work interval stayed open. Reconciled timing notes kept Oakley Brooks's work interval at clear. Instruments tracing Val Sato's action left the chemical response dormant. When Winter Cohen acted, the chemical response came back clear. Location review left Finley Meier's workshop room stable. Sequence notes placed Parker Meier's treatment order at stable. At sequence review, Oakley Brooks's treatment order stayed clear. Token and seal checks left Val Sato's tool stamp at clear. The sealed check showed Winter Cohen's tool stamp as open.
scenes.title: Reconstruction 4

scenes.prose: The inquiry moved from recollection to checked records. For this incident, the accepted tally was 67. The final definition was strict: the certified restoration lead was the one person whose six-stream tally equaled the accepted tally.
